summary: The Sun's six-year period turns on the Sun's strength. A strong, well-placed Sun brings wealth, honour from government and people in power, rank, children, fame and steady effort. A weak or afflicted Sun brings loss of money, displeasure of authorities, quarrels with relatives, worry about the father, fevers and moves away from home.
themes: travel and moves away from home
common_outcomes: when strong: wealth, happiness and honours from the government; gains of clothes, conveyances and produce (BPHS 47.7-11)
when strong: sons, intelligence, wisdom, status, knowledge, wealth, fame, valour and divine blessings (Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6)
when strong: courage, effort, intelligence, fame and valour grow; gains through fire, medicines, forests and royal contact (Saravali 41.25-26)
when well placed: wealth earned through hard work, travel, dealings with rulers, fame, steady devotion to duty (Phaladeepika 19.6)
when weak or afflicted: loss of wealth, anger of rulers, quarrels with kinsmen, distress to the father, trouble at home (BPHS 47.12-15; Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6)
when badly placed: quarrels, sudden anger of the ruler, illness among relatives, wandering, anxiety, fire danger to wealth, children and wife (Phaladeepika 19.5)
rare_outcomes: a high post such as army command through the ruler's favour (BPHS 47.7-11)
kingdom or royal insignia when the Sun is exalted or in the lagna (Saravali 41.54-59)
exile or banishment, punishment from government (BPHS 47.12-15)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] when the Sun is debilitated in the sign but exalted in the navamsa, at the end of the period (Jataka Parijata 18.72)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] in the period of any planet placed in the 8th house (Saravali 41.66-68)

by_area.personality: Courage, effort, intelligence and firmness grow when the Sun is strong (Saravali 41.25-26; Phaladeepika 19.6). When weak: anxiety, harsh temper and a turn to wrong acts (Phaladeepika 19.5; Saravali 41.27-28).
by_area.career: The main theme. Strong Sun: honours and a high post from government, even army command (BPHS 47.7-11); kingdom or leadership of large areas in exaltation, own sign or moolatrikona (Saravali 41.54-59). Weak Sun: punishment or displeasure from authorities, loss of position, humiliation (BPHS 47.12-15; Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6; Saravali 41.70).
by_area.finance: Wealth, produce, clothes and conveyances when strong (BPHS 47.7-11; Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6). Loss of wealth when weak (BPHS 47.12-15); efforts go to waste (Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6). Raman by sign: losses in Virgo, Libra, Capricorn and Aquarius; gains in most other signs (HPA ch. XXIV).
by_area.health: Weak Sun: fever, heart and bile problems, hunger and thirst (Saravali 41.27-28); eye, head and fever trouble when debilitated, eye and face trouble in an enemy sign (Saravali 41.54-59); the whole body suffers when the Sun is in the 8th (Saravali 41.54-59). Ill-health with enemies when weak (Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6).
by_area.relationships: Weak Sun: trouble through wife, children and relatives (Saravali 41.27-28); fire danger to wife and children (Phaladeepika 19.5). Raman: death of the wife with the Sun in Aquarius; enjoyment and friendships in Aries (HPA ch. XXIV).
by_area.family: Distress to the father and to paternal and maternal uncles, opposition from kinsmen, trouble at home when the Sun is weak (BPHS 47.12-15). A son when the Sun is joined with the 5th lord (BPHS 47.9). Jataka Parijata: the father falls ill at the start of the period (18.71).
by_area.spirituality: Righteous conduct with the Sun in Leo; reverence for holy people with the Sun in Taurus; pilgrimages with positional strength (Raman, HPA ch. XXIV). Divine blessings when strong (Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6).

strengtheners: Sun exalted, moolatrikona or in its own sign (BPHS 47.7; Saravali 41.54-59)
Sun in the lagna, a kendra or the 11th (BPHS 47.7-11); in the lagna gives a kingdom (Saravali 41.54-59)
Sun joined with the 9th or 10th lord, strong in its own vargas (BPHS 47.7-8)
benefic aspect on an otherwise afflicted Sun gives some relief (BPHS 47.15)
Sun as lord of the 8th is not harmed by that lordship (Phaladeepika 20.41)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Sun joined with malefics, Rahu or Ketu, or with the lord of the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.12, Santhanam and Sanskrit gloss)
malefic aspect on the Sun keeps the results bad (BPHS 47.15)
Sun exalted in the sign but in its debilitation navamsa (Jataka Parijata 18.72)
lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS judges this period from the lagna and by the Sun's dignity and associations; it gives no separate rule counted from the Moon. The Moon rules found (Phaladeepika 20.60-61, Jataka Parijata 18.7 and 18.14, Saravali 41.17-18) use the Moon's transit position when the period starts, counted from the dasha lord, so they need transit data rather than birth-chart facts. The Sun rules one sign (Leo), so its functional role depends on the lagna: Phaladeepika 20.41 says the Sun gives good results even as 8th lord (Capricorn lagna). Uttara Kalamrita 6.22 gives the general rule that kendra and trikona lords' periods are good and 6th, 8th and 12th lords' periods are hard.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.3-6 and 47.7-15, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2
source_views.view: Results come at the start, middle or end of a period by the planet's drekkana (first, second, third), reversed if retrograde. Good if the dasha lord is in the lagna, exalted, own or friendly sign; bad in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or in an enemy sign. Sun in own sign, exaltation, a kendra or the 11th, with the 9th or 10th lord and strong in varga: wealth, happiness, government honours. With the 5th lord a son; with the 2nd lord wealth; with the 4th lord conveyances; a high post like army chief. Debilitated, weak in 6/8/12, with malefics or the 6/8/12 lord: loss of wealth, punishment from government, exile, opposition of kinsmen, distress to the father and to uncles, trouble at home, needless enmity. Benefic aspect gives some good at times; malefic aspect keeps it bad.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.1-15, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Same structure. Verse 12 adds a Sun joined with Rahu or Ketu among the afflictions. Verse 15 says a benefic aspect brings some happiness in the middle of the period.

Badly placed Sun: quarrels, sudden anger of the ruler, illness of relatives, wandering, great anxiety, fire danger to wealth, grain, sons and wife. Well placed: wealth through harsh effort, journeys, dealings with kings and disputes, travel through forests and hills, fame, success in business, steady devotion to duty. Ch. 20 adds general rules: exalted, own or friendly sign good, debilitated, inimical or 6/8/12 bad (20.14); the Sun as 8th lord still good (20.41); planets in shirshodaya signs act early in a period, prishtodaya late (20.33).

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.71-72 and 18.58 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri vol. 2)
source_views.view: Start of the Sun's period: the father falls ill and expenses are heavy; middle: trouble to everyone in the household, people and animals; end: ease and comfort. Sun exalted but in its debilitation navamsa: blame, danger, death of a son, wife or paternal relative, loss in farming. Sun debilitated but in its exaltation navamsa: regal prosperity and happiness, though loss of wealth or the native's own death may come near the end. For any malefic planet, its dignity shows at the start of its period, its house matters in the middle and aspects on it at the end (18.58).

source_views.source: Saravali 41.25-28, 41.53-59, 41.66-75 (English text, lakshminarayanlenasia.com PDF; translator not named)
source_views.view: Favourable Sun: gains from forests, medicines, travel, fire and royal contact; courage, diligence, intelligence and fame grow; kingship. Adverse Sun: grief through servants, theft, eyes, weapons, fire, water and the king; trouble from children, wife and relatives; fever, heart and bile disorders. By placement: lagna gives kingdom; other kendras in an enemy's sign give hip, throat and eye trouble; debilitated gives eye, fever and head trouble and confinement; exalted gives kingdom and insignia; moolatrikona ends miseries and gives leadership of large areas; enemy sign gives eye and face trouble and disgrace; 8th house afflicts the whole body and causes wandering. General rules: planets in the 6th give misfortune, in the 8th death; planets in shirshodaya signs act at the start of their period, prishtodaya and debilitated ones at the end.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6 (tr. S.S. Sareen; also P.S. Sastri ed.)
source_views.view: Auspiciously placed Sun: sons, intelligence, wisdom, status and power, knowledge, wealth, fame, valour, happiness and divine favour. Inauspiciously placed: hardship, wasted effort, loss of money and position, disease and enemies, royal displeasure, ill-health of the father.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 231-234
source_views.view: Results by the Sun's sign: Aries (deep exaltation) sudden gains, travel east, foreign residence, quarrels with friends, pleasures; moolatrikona children, respect, power and political success; Taurus land and reverence for saints; Gemini wealth, learning, music; Cancer political success and property; Leo respect from the great, righteous conduct, children; Virgo serious illness and losses; Libra poverty, enemies, failures, death of brothers and friends; Scorpio new enterprises, hill travel; Sagittarius success and health; Capricorn wandering, loss of patrimony and good name; Aquarius worry, death of wife, loss of property; Pisces wealth and celebrations. Also lists results by the six strengths (sthana, dig, kala, naisargika, chesta).

source_views.source: V.G. Rele, Directional Astrology of the Hindus, pp. 67-72
source_views.view: General method: a planet in dignity (exalted, own or friendly sign, with benefics, with the lagna, 9th or 10th lord, in angles, trines or the 11th) gives good results in its period; in debility (fall, enemy sign, with malefics, ruling 3/6/8/11) gives evil. Gives graded results for the nine avasthas, including Kopita, a planet joined with the Sun: sinful conduct, disgrace, eye trouble, danger from fire, king and thieves.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, pp. 202-203
source_views.view: The major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects; the major lord sets the general nature of the time. A good period does not always give its fruit at once: the seeds show at the start. The beginning of a period is the time for remedies: strengthen a weak benefic lord with its gem, propitiate a malefic one by mantra, ritual or worship.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 16.5.1
source_views.view: A planet gives in its period the results promised by its positions in the divisional charts (for example the D-10 for career), not only the rasi chart.

disagreements: Phases: Jataka Parijata 18.71 gives a fixed pattern for the Sun's period (father ill and expenses at the start, household trouble in the middle, ease at the end); BPHS 47.3-4 instead times results by the Sun's drekkana; Saravali 41.75 and Phaladeepika 20.33 by whether the sign rises head-first or hind-first. Santhanam's BPHS 47.15 says a benefic aspect gives good 'at times'; the Sanskrit gloss puts that relief in the middle of the period. Raman's sign list makes the Sun in Virgo, Capricorn and Aquarius (signs that are neither enemy nor debilitation for the Sun in BPHS) quite bad, which the BPHS dignity rules do not predict.
phrasing_guidance: Frame this as a period about authority, recognition and self-reliance whose tone depends on the Sun's strength. For a weak Sun, advise patience with superiors and government matters, care of health (fever, eyes, heart) and attention to the father's wellbeing. Do not state that a parent, spouse or the native will die; turn maraka lines into advice about caution and health checks.

remedies.source: Frawley, Astrology of the Seers p. 203 (general rule for any period lord)

phases: Jataka Parijata 18.71: at the start the father falls ill and expenses are heavy; in the middle everyone in the household, people and animals, has trouble; at the end there is ease and comfort. BPHS 47.3-4: if the Sun is in the first drekkana (0-10 degrees) of its sign its results come at the start of the period, in the second drekkana in the middle, in the third at the end (reversed if retrograde, which the Sun never is). Saravali 41.75 and Phaladeepika 20.33: a planet in a shirshodaya (head-rising) sign gives its results early, in a prishtodaya (hind-rising) sign or debilitated late, in Pisces (both) throughout or in the middle. Jataka Parijata 18.58: for a malefic such as the Sun, its dignity shows at the start, its house in the middle and the aspects on it at the end.
